gaps.why_now: The roadmap names an Architecture Council review process, but the live repo needed a reviewable process note that says when council review is required and what packet it must carry.
A dedicated manifest keeps the governance slice explicit and machine-checkable instead of burying the scope inside prose.
The Phase 15 review-process note should stay runnable so future edits do not quietly drop required trigger, packet, or decision-bucket language.
The review-process packet now needs one reusable fill-in artifact so freeze-map status reviews stop inventing ad hoc field order and reviewer-facing evidence layout.
The live review checklist still needs one explicit prompt that links freeze-map status-change requests back to the Architecture Council review record and decision bucket.
The shared Phase 15 build gate should keep the review-process test aligned with the freeze-map governance test so the governance lane stays coherent.
The landed Phase 15 parity scorecard is the live evidence attachment point for Architecture Council requests instead of a planned follow-up.
The review-process packet standardizes where each frozen anchor stores Council decision records, blocker dispositions, benchmark notes, and replay commands.
The review-process note records the retained `retired_from_active_discussion` closeout state and the reopen triggers that keep a stay-in-C outcome reviewable without implying approval.
The review-process note names the bounded reopen-trigger catalog so later exception records and scorecard updates reuse the same stay-in-C reopen vocabulary.

The shared checklist and freeze map already required the approver-set, rollback-threshold, and indefinite-C-policy fields, so the review-process note and its manifest needed a bounded sync to keep the Architecture Council packet truthful.
